The *Jatukaṇṇittheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 411) is a verse text preserved in the *Therāpadāna* section of the Pali canon [SuttaCentral]. It relates the past-life deeds and spiritual biography of the senior monk Jatukaṇṇi (Jatukaṇṇin). SuttaCentral records five translations across five modern languages [SuttaCentral].

Text-reuse analysis by DharmaNexus detects extensive intertextual sharing across Pali literature, identifying 207 matching passages shared with 29 Pali texts [DharmaNexus]. The most substantial reuse partners are the first and second parts of the commentary to the *Theragāthā* (*Theragāthā-aṭṭhakathā*), which share extended stretches of verse (especially segments §42.1–44.4) [DharmaNexus]. Formulaic and thematic verse segments are also shared with multiple other apadānas, including the *Upasivattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 407), *Bhaddālittheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 413), *Upālittheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 8), *Upavānattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 562 and Tha-Ap 24), and *Dhotakattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 406) [DharmaNexus].

Beyond Pali, DharmaNexus automatically aligns the text with several Sanskrit and Tibetan Buddhist works [DharmaNexus]. The strongest alignment occurs with the Sanskrit *Kaṭhināvadāna*, showing a high-scoring parallel to segments §41.2–41.3 [DharmaNexus]. Additional lower-scoring alignments occur with Tibetan translations in the Kangyur and Tengyur, such as the *Vinayavastu* (D0001-2), the *Suvarṇaprabhāsottama-sūtra* (D0557), the *Mahāvyutpatti* (D4346), and the *Ārya-avalokana-sūtra* (D0195) [DharmaNexus].
